Lesko_Help_HC02_Stress_Mental_Health_Qui.text:
Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Stress & Mental Health
Feeling overwhelmed, anxious, or down? Support is available — from free counseling to low-cost
therapy and self-help tools. You don’t need to be in crisis to ask for help. Below are trusted national
starting points.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

If you’re in crisis right now, call or text 988. Otherwise, the resources below help you find ongoing,
affordable mental health support. Most health insurance and Medicaid cover mental health care.

1

Find Affordable Therapy & Counseling

Free and low-cost mental health care exists — including sliding-scale clinics that charge based on income.

FindSupport.gov
A government guide to finding the right mental health support and understanding your options.
→ www.findsupport.gov

FindTreatment.gov
Search for low-cost and sliding-scale mental health and substance-use providers near you.
→ www.findtreatment.gov

Community Mental Health Centers (SAMHSA)
Find federally supported centers that provide care regardless of ability to pay.
→ www.samhsa.gov/find-help

2 Free Support Groups

Peer support from people who understand — free and available across the country and online.

NAMI — National Alliance on Mental Illness
Free support groups, education, and a helpline for people and families. Call or text the NAMI HelpLine.
→ www.nami.org/help 1-800-950-6264

Mental Health America — Find Support
Free screening tools and a directory of local affiliates and support.
→ www.mhanational.org/finding-help

3 Free Self-Help Tools

Trusted, no-cost tools for managing stress, anxiety, and low mood between appointments.

Mindfulness, CBT & VA Mental Health Apps
The VA’s free, public mental health apps (like Mindfulness Coach and CBT-i Coach) are free to anyone, not
only veterans.
→ mobile.va.gov/appstore/mental-health

CDC — Coping With Stress
Plain, trustworthy guidance on managing stress and protecting your mental health.
→ www.cdc.gov/mental-health/living-with/index.html

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Be cautious of apps or sites promising to “cure”
anxiety or depression with special sound
frequencies, supplements, or paid programs — these
aren’t proven. Stick to licensed providers and the
trusted nonprofits above.

Ask your doctor or insurance about covered mental
health visits — many plans include several free or
low-cost sessions. A primary care doctor can also
be a good first step and refer you onward.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Need ongoing local support?

This guide covers national starting points. For therapists, support groups, and low-cost clinics near you —
including sliding-scale options — use the personalized AI search or ask in the Questions area, and we’ll help
you find the right fit.

Lesko_Help_VET_6_Housing_Home_Loans_Quic.tip:
Watch for lenders pushing needless VA loan
refinances (“churning”) that add fees — only
refinance if it clearly saves you money. And never
pay for your COE; it’s free on VA.gov.

Get your Certificate of Eligibility before house-
hunting, and shop several VA-approved lenders —
rates and fees vary, and disabled veterans should
confirm their funding-fee exemption.

the box once you’ve checked each one.

saving you hundreds a month. Disabled veterans are often exempt from the funding fee. Getting your
eligibility certificate is free.

1 Buy or Refinance a Home

Powerful loan benefits with no down payment.

VA Home Loan
Zero down payment, no PMI, competitive rates. Start by getting your Certificate of Eligibility.
→ www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans

Get Your Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Prove your VA loan eligibility — free and often instant on VA.gov.
→ www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/how-to-apply

Grants to make a home livable with a disability.

Adapted Housing Grants (SAH/SHA)
Grants to buy or modify a home for a service-connected disability.
→ www.va.gov/housing-assistance/disability-housing-grants

Home Improvement (HISA) Grants
VA grants for medically necessary home modifications.
→ www.prosthetics.va.gov/psas/HISA2.asp

3 Keep Your Home

Free help if you’re behind on your mortgage.

VA Loan Trouble? Get Help
If you have a VA loan and are struggling, VA loan technicians can help you avoid foreclosure. Call the VA.
→ www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/trouble-making-payments 1-877-827-3702

4 If You’re Homeless or At Risk

Immediate, free help with housing.

National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
Free 24/7 help if you’re homeless or at risk of becoming homeless.
→ www.va.gov/homeless 1-877-424-3838

HUD-VASH & SSVF
Housing vouchers and support services for veterans. Ask the call center above.
→ www.va.gov/homeless/hud-vash.asp

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Watch for lenders pushing needless VA loan
refinances (“churning”) that add fees — only
refinance if it clearly saves you money. And never
pay for your COE; it’s free on VA.gov.

Get your Certificate of Eligibility before house-
hunting, and shop several VA-approved lenders —
rates and fees vary, and disabled veterans should
confirm their funding-fee exemption.

Lesko_Help_CB_B01_Nonprofit_Registration.text:
Q U I C K G U I D E · L A U N C H A N O N P R O F I T

Nonprofit Registration Checklist
Want to start a nonprofit? The path to official 501(c)(3) status is a clear set of steps — and you can do
most of it yourself. Below is the checklist with official resources. Tick the box once you’ve done each
one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

You do NOT need to pay a company thousands to start a nonprofit — the IRS and your state let you do it
directly. If your group is small, a “fiscal sponsor” can even let you operate under another nonprofit’s
status first.

1 Build the Foundation

Set up the legal bones of your nonprofit.

Define Mission & Recruit a Board
Write a clear mission and recruit a board of directors (most states require at least 3).
→ www.councilofnonprofits.org/running-nonprofit/governance-leadership/board-roles-and-
responsibilities

Incorporate in Your State
File articles of incorporation with your state, and create bylaws. SBA links to your state office.
→ www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/register-your-business

2 Get Your Federal IDs

You need an EIN and then tax-exempt status from the IRS.

Get an EIN — Free From the IRS
Your nonprofit’s federal tax ID. Always free at IRS.gov.
→ www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/apply-for-an-employer-identification-
number-ein-online

Apply for 501(c)(3) Status
File IRS Form 1023 (or the shorter, cheaper 1023-EZ if you qualify) to become tax-exempt.
→ www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/applying-for-tax-exempt-status

3 Register to Operate & Fundraise

A few more registrations keep you legal and able to raise money.

Register for Charitable Solicitation
Most states require nonprofits to register before fundraising. Check your state’s rules.
→ www.councilofnonprofits.org/running-nonprofit/fundraising-and-resource-development/
charitable-solicitation-registration

Open a Nonprofit Bank Account
Once incorporated with an EIN, open a dedicated bank account to keep finances clean.
→ Open after incorporation & EIN

4 Get Free Help

Experienced advisors guide you through the whole process.

SCORE — Nonprofit Mentoring
Free mentors who’ve started nonprofits before.
→ www.score.org

National Council of Nonprofits
Free, trusted guidance for every step of starting and running a nonprofit.
→ www.councilofnonprofits.org

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Companies charge $1,000–$3,000 to do paperwork
you can file yourself for under $300 in fees. The IRS
Form 1023-EZ is short and inexpensive if you qualify
— check before paying anyone.

If you’re testing an idea, consider a “fiscal sponsor”
— an existing 501(c)(3) that lets you operate under
their status. It’s faster and cheaper than full
incorporation while you get started.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Need help where you live?

This guide covers national steps. For your state’s exact incorporation and fundraising rules, use the
personalized AI search or ask in the Questions area, and we’ll point you to the right offices.

Lesko_Help_VET_2_Getting_Started_VSO_Qui.title: Getting Started — VSO & First Steps
Lesko_Help_VET_2_Getting_Started_VSO_Qui.tip:
Avoid for-profit “claim consultants” that charge fees
or a percentage of your back pay — accredited
VSOs do the same work free. Charging upfront for VA
claim prep is against federal rules.

Gather your DD-214 and any medical records before
your VSO appointment — the more evidence you
bring, the faster and stronger your claim. File an
intent to file the same day.

resources.description: The smartest first move as a veteran is getting free, expert help and gathering your records. Below is how to start strong. Tick the box once you’ve done each one. A free accredited VSO is your single best resource — they know the system, file claims at no cost, and dramatically improve your odds. Don’t go it alone, and never pay for claim help. 1 Get Your Free Representative Accredited help that costs nothing and works for you. Find an Accredited VSO Officers from groups like the American Legion, DAV, and VFW file your claims for free.

Getting Started — VSO & First Steps
The smartest first move as a veteran is getting free, expert help and gathering your records. Below is
how to start strong. Tick the box once you’ve done each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

A free accredited VSO is your single best resource — they know the system, file claims at no cost, and
dramatically improve your odds. Don’t go it alone, and never pay for claim help.

1 Get Your Free Representative

Accredited help that costs nothing and works for you.

Find an Accredited VSO
Officers from groups like the American Legion, DAV, and VFW file your claims for free.
→ www.va.gov/get-help-from-accredited-representative

VA Hotline
Call the VA directly with any benefits question.
→ www.va.gov 1-800-827-1000

2 Set Up Your Accounts

Get digital access to your benefits and records.

Create a VA.gov Account
Manage claims, messages, prescriptions, and records online.
→ www.va.gov

Get Your DD-214 & Records
Your discharge papers prove eligibility. Request them free from the National Archives.
→ www.archives.gov/veterans/military-service-records

Your discharge status affects benefits — and can sometimes be upgraded.

Check & Upgrade Your Discharge
A less-than-honorable discharge may still qualify, or be upgradable. Free help is available.
→ www.va.gov/discharge-upgrade-instructions

4 Protect Your Effective Date

One quick step preserves your back pay.

File an Intent to File
Filing this on VA.gov locks in an earlier start date for benefits while you prepare your claim.
→ www.va.gov/disability/how-to-file-claim

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Avoid for-profit “claim consultants” that charge fees
or a percentage of your back pay — accredited
VSOs do the same work free. Charging upfront for VA
claim prep is against federal rules.

Gather your DD-214 and any medical records before
your VSO appointment — the more evidence you
bring, the faster and stronger your claim. File an
intent to file the same day.

Q U I C K G U I D E · TA X E S H E L P G U I D A N C E

Property & State Tax Relief
Property and state taxes can be a heavy burden — but many people qualify for exemptions, freezes,
and rebates they never claim. Below is how to find relief. Tick the box once you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Most property-tax relief comes from your state, county, or town — and you usually have to apply.
Seniors, veterans, people with disabilities, and lower-income homeowners often qualify. Applying is free.

1 Common Property Tax Breaks

Programs that lower or freeze what you owe on your home.

Homestead Exemption
Most states reduce property tax on your primary home. Ask your county assessor how to apply.
→ Ask your county tax assessor

Senior & Disability Freezes/Exemptions
Many areas freeze or cut property taxes for seniors and people with disabilities.
→ Ask your county tax assessor

2 Relief for Specific Groups

Extra breaks for veterans and lower-income homeowners.

Veteran Property Tax Exemptions
Many states reduce or eliminate property tax for eligible veterans, especially disabled veterans.
→ www.va.gov/resources/property-tax-exemptions-for-veterans

Circuit Breaker & Rebate Programs
Many states offer rebates when property tax is high relative to income. Search your state + “property tax
rebate.”
→ Search your state + 'property tax relief'

3

If You’re Behind on Property Tax

Options to avoid losing your home to a tax sale.

Payment Plans & Deferrals
Many counties let you pay overdue property tax over time, or defer it for seniors. Ask your tax office
before a tax sale.
→ Ask your county tax office

Free Legal Help
If you face a tax foreclosure, legal aid may help. See the Free Legal Help & Legal Aid guide.
→ www.lawhelp.org

4 Challenge an Unfair Assessment

If your home is over-valued, you may be overpaying.

Appeal Your Property Assessment
If your assessed value seems too high, you can appeal it — often free. Ask your assessor about the
deadline.
→ Ask your county assessor about appeals

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Watch for companies offering to “lower your
property taxes” for a big fee — you can usually apply
for exemptions and appeals yourself for free through
your county. Never pay to “claim” a rebate you can
get directly.

Check with your county assessor every year —
exemptions aren’t always automatic, and deadlines
matter. A single homestead or senior exemption can
save hundreds annually.

payment to hand over a car.

application updated — waitlists are long and need is
weighed heavily. A short letter explaining how a car
gets you to work can make your case stronger.

These national nonprofits refurbish donated vehicles and give them to qualifying families, often for work or
medical need.

Free Charity Cars / 1-800-Charity Cars
The nation’s oldest and largest car-donation charity. Apply online; priority for survivors, veterans, and
families with urgent need.
→ www.800charitycars.org

Working Cars for Working Families (NCLC)
A national directory of car-ownership programs — the best tool to find a local group that gives or finances
cars near you.
→ www.workingcarsforworkingfamilies.org

Vehicles for Change
Provides low-cost cars to working families in the areas it serves, and runs auto-training programs.
→ www.vehiclesforchange.org

2 Help Through Local Programs

State and local programs sometimes provide cars or transportation help tied to work or job training.

TANF — Work-Related Transportation
If you get TANF (cash assistance), your state may help with a car, repairs, or transport to work. Ask your
caseworker.
→ www.acf.hhs.gov/ofa/programs/tanf/about

211 — Local Vehicle & Ride Help
Call or search for local car-donation programs, gas cards, and transportation help.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

3 Get to Medical Care

If your need is getting to doctor visits, there’s free non-emergency medical transportation for many people.

Medicaid Non-Emergency Medical Transportation
If you have Medicaid, you may get free rides to medical appointments. Ask your state Medicaid office or
plan.
→ www.medicaid.gov/medicaid/benefits/non-emergency-medical-transportation

Eldercare Locator — Senior Rides
Connects older adults to local transportation services and ride programs.
→ eldercare.acl.gov or call 1-800-677-1110

4 Everyday Ride Help

For getting to work or job interviews while you wait for a car.

Local Public Transit Reduced Fares
Most transit agencies offer reduced fares for seniors, people with disabilities, and low-income riders. Ask
your local transit office.
→ Ask your local transit agency

United Way / Ride United
In many areas, United Way partners on rides to work, interviews, and appointments. Ask 211.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

If a “free car” offer asks for a fee, gift card, or your
bank login to “release” the vehicle, it’s a scam. Real
charities never charge to apply and never ask for
payment to hand over a car.

Apply to more than one car charity and keep your
application updated — waitlists are long and need is
weighed heavily. A short letter explaining how a car
gets you to work can make your case stronger.

Lesko_Help_10_Car_Repair_Vehicle_Help_Qu.title: Car Repair & Vehicle Help
Lesko_Help_10_Car_Repair_Vehicle_Help_Qu.tip:
Government car-repair help is a top target for
scams. Never pay a fee to apply, and don’t trust a
caller who “guarantees” a repair grant. Real programs
are free and ask for proof of income and need.

Get a written, itemized estimate from a licensed
mechanic first — most programs require it, and it
helps you avoid being overcharged. Explain you need
the car for work; many programs prioritize
employment.

Set aside about 25–30% of gig income for taxes and
pay quarterly — many new gig workers get a nasty
surprise at tax time. The IRS Gig Center explains

or simple spreadsheet works). Deductions can cut
your tax bill significantly — but only if you have
records.

smarter, save on taxes, and grow. Below are trusted national resources. Tick the box once you’ve

As a gig worker you’re self-employed, which means taxes and benefits work differently. The resources

1 Handle Taxes the Right Way

IRS — Gig Economy Tax Center
Official guidance on taxes, deductions, and quarterly payments for gig workers.
→ www.irs.gov/businesses/gig-economy-tax-center

→ www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/deducting-business-expenses

You can get health coverage and save for retirement on your own.

Self-employed people often qualify for subsidized health plans.
→ www.healthcare.gov/self-employed/coverage

Tax-advantaged retirement accounts built for self-employed people.
→ www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/retirement-plans-for-self-employed-people

3 Grow & Formalize

Turn gig income into a real, protected business.

Consider an LLC
Forming an LLC can protect you and look more professional. See the First Legal Steps guide.
→ See: First Legal Steps guide

Free Business Mentoring
SCORE mentors help freelancers and gig workers grow and stabilize income.
→ www.score.org

4 Find Gig & Freelance Work

Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Medical Debt Relief
Already have medical debt — maybe in collections? You have rights and real options to reduce or
erase it. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Medical debt is treated differently from other debt, and you have strong protections. Don’t rush to pay a
collector before checking whether the bill qualifies for charity care or whether it’s even valid.

1 Try to Erase the Debt First

Even debt in collections may still qualify for hospital charity care, which can wipe it out.

Dollar For — Charity Care
Free help applying for hospital financial assistance — it can forgive bills you already owe.
→ dollarfor.org

Undue Medical Debt
A nonprofit that buys and erases medical debt — you can’t apply directly, but learn how it works and who
it helps.
→ unduemedicaldebt.org

2 Know Your Rights

Federal protections limit what collectors can do and keep most medical debt off your credit report.

CFPB — Medical Debt Rights
Learn your rights, including new rules keeping most medical bills off credit reports. File a complaint if a
collector breaks the rules.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/medical-debt

Dispute Errors & Validate the Debt
You can demand a collector prove a medical debt is yours and correct. Many medical debts have errors.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-validation-letter-en-2113

3 Get Free Advice

Free, trustworthy counseling and legal help for dealing with medical debt.

Nonprofit Credit Counseling (NFCC)
Free or low-cost counseling to build a plan for medical and other debt.
→ www.nfcc.org

Free Legal Aid
If a collector is suing you or garnishing wages, free legal aid may help.
→ www.lawhelp.org

4 Negotiate What You Owe

Medical debt is often negotiable, especially if you can offer a one-time payment.

Negotiate a Lower Amount
Collectors often accept far less than the full balance. Offer a lump sum and get any agreement in writing
before paying.
→ Get any settlement in writing first

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Don’t pay a medical collector before checking your
rights — many medical debts are wrong, already off
your credit report, or eligible for charity care. Never
give a collector bank access; pay only with a written
agreement.

Always get debt settlements in writing before you
pay a cent. And apply for the hospital’s charity care
even on old debt — getting the original bill forgiven is
better than negotiating with a collector.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Q U I C K G U I D E · TA X E S H E L P G U I D A N C E

Tax Credits You May Be Missing
Tax credits can mean thousands of dollars back — even if you owe no tax or didn’t earn much. Many
people miss them. Below are the big ones and how to claim them. Tick the box once you’ve checked
each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Refundable credits can put money in your pocket even with little or no income — but only if you file a
return. A free VITA preparer (see the Free Tax Filing guide) can make sure you get every credit.

1 Credits for Workers & Families

The biggest refundable credits — real cash back.

Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
Worth up to ~$8,000 for low-to-moderate-income workers. Many eligible people never claim it.
→ www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/earned-income-tax-credit-eitc

Child Tax Credit
Up to $2,200 per qualifying child, with part refundable. Check if you qualify.
→ www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/child-tax-credit

Child & Dependent Care Credit
Helps cover the cost of child care or care for a dependent so you can work.
→ www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/child-and-dependent-care-credit-information

2 Credits for School & Learning

Education credits lower the cost of college and training.

American Opportunity & Lifetime Learning Credits
Credits for college and continuing-education costs — for you or your kids.
→ www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/education-credits-aotc-llc

3 Credits for Savers & Home

Often-missed credits for retirement saving and energy upgrades.

Saver’s Credit
A credit just for putting money into a retirement account, if your income qualifies.
→ www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/plan-participant-employee/retirement-savings-contributions-
savers-credit

Energy Home Credits
Credits for certain energy-saving home improvements. Confirm current rules, as these change.
→ www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/home-energy-tax-credits

4 Claim Credits From Past Years

You may be able to get money from returns you didn’t file.

File Back Returns for Missed Refunds
You generally have up to 3 years to file and still claim a refund or credit. A free clinic or VITA site can help.
→ www.irs.gov/filing

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

You don’t need to pay anyone to “find” your credits
— free VITA preparers and tax software apply them
automatically. Be wary of preparers who invent
credits you don’t qualify for; that can trigger an
audit.

Always file a tax return even if you didn’t earn much
or owe nothing — refundable credits like the EITC are
only paid out if you file. It’s often free money left on
the table.

Q U I C K G U I D E · PAY D E B T & B I L L S

Utility Assistance — Energy & Water
Behind on gas, electric, heating, or water? You may qualify for federal and local programs that help pay
what you owe and keep your service on. Below are the most trusted national starting points. Tick the
box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Call your utility company first and ask for their hardship program, payment plan, or budget billing — and
tell them if you’ve had a shut-off notice. Then apply to the programs below. A real assistance program
never charges a fee just to apply.

1

Federal Energy Bill Help (LIHEAP)

LIHEAP is the main federal program for heating, cooling, and electricity costs. You apply through your state or
local Community Action Agency.

LIHEAP — Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
Helps pay heating and cooling bills, and in many states helps during an energy crisis or shut-off. Find your
state’s program and how to apply.
→ www.acf.hhs.gov/ocs/programs/liheap

LIHEAP Help Line
Call to find the office that takes applications in your area.
→ 1-866-674-6327 National Energy Assistance Referral

2 Help With Your Water Bill

The federal water assistance program (LIHWAP) has ended, so water help now comes from your water
company and local agencies. These are the best places to start.

Your Water Company — Hardship & Payment Plans
Most water utilities have low-income discounts, payment plans, or shut-off protection. Call the number
on your bill and ask what they offer.
→ Call the number on your water bill

211 — Local Water & Utility Help
Call or search to find local programs that help with overdue water and utility bills.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

3 Local Hands-On Help

Community agencies and charities help you apply, cover emergency bills, and prevent shut-offs — often for
several utilities at once.

Community Action Agency — Find Yours
Local agencies run LIHEAP and other utility help, and can walk you through applying.
→ communityactionpartnership.com/find-a-cap

Dollar Energy Fund
Works with utility companies to help pay overdue energy and water bills.
→ www.dollarenergy.org

Salvation Army — Utility Assistance
Local branches may help with emergency utility bills. Availability depends on funding.
→ www.salvationarmyusa.org

4 Lower Your Bills For Good (Weatherization)

Free home energy upgrades — insulation, weather-sealing, repairs — that permanently cut your energy bills.
No cost to eligible households.

Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)
Free energy-saving improvements for income-eligible homes. Find how to apply in your state.
→ www.energy.gov/scep/wap/how-apply-weatherization-assistance

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Old websites still list “LIHWAP” water grants — that
federal program ended and is no longer taking
applications. Use your water company and 211
instead.

Apply before you’re disconnected. Many programs
offer emergency help or can stop a shut-off if you
reach out in time. Funds often run out, so apply early
in the season.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Ask for your personalized utility search

This guide covers the main national programs. For help specific to your city, county, or ZIP code — including
your local utility’s own programs — use the personalized AI search or ask in the Questions area, and we’ll help
you find the closest options and apply.

Lesko_Help_TL_A2_Tax_Debt_IRS_Relief_Qui.title: Tax Debt & IRS Relief
Lesko_Help_TL_A2_Tax_Debt_IRS_Relief_Qui.watch_out:
“tax relief” companies on TV that charge huge fees for things you can do yourself for free or cheap.

1 Set Up a Payment Plan

The IRS lets most people pay over time, often online in minutes.

IRS Online Payment Plan
Apply online to pay your balance over months or years. Most people qualify.
→ www.irs.gov/payments/online-payment-agreement-application

Short-Term Extension
Need just a little time? You can request up to 180 extra days to pay.
→ www.irs.gov/payments

2 Settle for Less Than You Owe

If you truly can’t pay, the IRS may accept a reduced amount.

Offer in Compromise
Settle your tax debt for less than the full amount if you qualify. Use the free pre-qualifier tool first.
→ www.irs.gov/payments/offer-in-compromise

Currently Not Collectible
If paying would leave you unable to cover basics, the IRS may pause collection.
→ www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/temporarily-delay-the-collection-
process

3 Get Free Expert Help

Free, independent help when you’re stuck with the IRS.

Taxpayer Advocate Service
A free, independent IRS office that helps when you have a hardship or can’t resolve an issue.
→ www.taxpayeradvocate.irs.gov 1-877-777-4778

Low Income Taxpayer Clinic (LITC)
Free legal help for disputes with the IRS if you’re low-income. See the Free Legal Help to Fight the IRS
guide.
→ www.taxpayeradvocate.irs.gov/litc

4 Reduce Penalties

You may be able to remove penalties you’ve been charged.

Penalty Relief / First-Time Abatement
If you usually file on time, the IRS may remove penalties. Just ask.
→ www.irs.gov/payments/penalty-relief

⚠ WATC H OUT FOR

★
Lesko_Help_TL_A2_Tax_Debt_IRS_Relief_Qui.tip:
Ignore TV and radio ads promising to “settle your IRS
debt for pennies” for a big upfront fee — most
people don’t qualify for that, and you can apply
yourself for free. A real Offer in Compromise is filed
directly with the IRS.

Always open and respond to IRS letters — ignoring
them leads to liens, levies, and garnished wages.
Even a phone call to set up a small payment plan
stops most collection actions.

→ www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/temporarily-delay-the-collection-
process

3 Get Free Expert Help

Free, independent help when you’re stuck with the IRS.

Taxpayer Advocate Service
A free, independent IRS office that helps when you have a hardship or can’t resolve an issue.
→ www.taxpayeradvocate.irs.gov 1-877-777-4778

Low Income Taxpayer Clinic (LITC)
Free legal help for disputes with the IRS if you’re low-income. See the Free Legal Help to Fight the IRS
guide.
→ www.taxpayeradvocate.irs.gov/litc

4 Reduce Penalties

You may be able to remove penalties you’ve been charged.

Penalty Relief / First-Time Abatement
If you usually file on time, the IRS may remove penalties. Just ask.
→ www.irs.gov/payments/penalty-relief

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Ignore TV and radio ads promising to “settle your IRS
debt for pennies” for a big upfront fee — most
people don’t qualify for that, and you can apply
yourself for free. A real Offer in Compromise is filed
directly with the IRS.

Always open and respond to IRS letters — ignoring
them leads to liens, levies, and garnished wages.
Even a phone call to set up a small payment plan
stops most collection actions.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

the personalized AI search or ask in the Questions area, and we’ll point you to free help.

Lesko_Help_HC06_Healthy_Food_Quick_Guide.text:
Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Healthy Food on a Budget
Eating well shouldn’t be a luxury. Federal programs, fresh-produce incentives, and nutrition help make
healthy food more affordable. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve
looked into each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Many of these programs stretch your food budget toward fresh, healthy choices — and you may qualify
even if you’re working. Applying is always free.

1 Get Help Buying Groceries

Federal benefits put money toward food each month — the foundation of eating well on a budget.

SNAP — Monthly Grocery Benefits
Money on a card for groceries, including fruits, vegetables, and healthy staples. Apply through your state.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility

WIC — Pregnant Women & Young Kids
Free healthy foods, formula, and nutrition support for families with children under 5.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/wic

2 Double Your Money on Fresh Produce

Programs that match your SNAP dollars when you buy fruits and vegetables.

SNAP at Farmers Markets & Double Up
Many markets double your SNAP spending on fresh produce. Find participating markets and Double Up
Food Bucks programs.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/farmers-markets

GusNIP Produce Incentives
Federal produce-incentive programs that stretch your fruit and vegetable budget. Find local programs.
→ www.nifa.usda.gov/grants/programs/hunger-food-security-programs/gus-schumacher-nutrition-
incentive-program

3 Free Food & Healthy Choices

Food banks increasingly offer fresh produce, and nutrition help is free.

Feeding America — Find Fresh Food
Many food banks now offer fresh produce, dairy, and proteins. Find one near you.
→ www.feedingamerica.org/find-your-local-foodbank

MyPlate — Free Healthy Eating Guide
Free, simple guidance and budget recipes from the USDA.
→ www.myplate.gov/eat-healthy/healthy-eating-budget

4 For Seniors & Families

Targeted programs help older adults and families afford healthy food.

Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program
Coupons for fresh produce at farmers markets for eligible older adults. Ask your local agency on aging.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/sfmnp

Eldercare Locator — Senior Meals
Connects older adults to congregate and home-delivered meal programs.
→ eldercare.acl.gov 1-800-677-1110

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Be skeptical of pricey “detox,” cleanse, or
supplement programs marketed as healthy eating.
Real, affordable nutrition comes from whole foods —
and the programs above help you afford them.

Shop the produce in season and check whether your
farmers market doubles SNAP dollars — it’s one of
the easiest ways to get more fresh fruits and
vegetables for your money.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

This guide covers national programs. For farmers markets, produce-incentive programs, and food help
specific to your area, use the personalized AI search or ask in the Questions area, and we’ll help you find
them.

Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Help for Caregivers
Caring for a loved one is a huge job — and you deserve support too. There’s free help, a break
(respite), and even ways to get paid for caregiving. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the
box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

You can’t pour from an empty cup. The resources below help you find support, take breaks, and in some
cases get paid for the care you provide. Start with the Eldercare Locator — it opens many doors.

1 Start Here — Find Local Support

One call connects you to local caregiver services, respite, and guidance.

Eldercare Locator
Connects you to local Area Agencies on Aging, caregiver support, and respite services.
→ eldercare.acl.gov 1-800-677-1110

Caregiver Action Network
Free education, a help desk, and peer support for family caregivers.
→ www.caregiveraction.org 1-855-227-3640

2 Get Paid for Caregiving

In many cases, family caregivers can receive payment through Medicaid or the VA.

Medicaid Self-Directed Care
Many states let people on Medicaid hire and pay a family member as their caregiver. Ask your state
Medicaid office.
→ www.medicaid.gov/medicaid/long-term-services-supports/self-directed-services

VA Caregiver Support
The VA offers stipends, training, and support for those caring for eligible veterans.
→ www.caregiver.va.gov 1-855-260-3274

Paid Family Leave (Your State)
A growing number of states offer paid leave to care for a seriously ill family member. Check your state’s
program.
→ www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla

3 Take a Break (Respite Care)

Respite gives you time to rest while your loved one is cared for safely.

ARCH Respite Locator
Find respite-care services that give caregivers a much-needed break.
→ archrespite.org/caregiver-resources/respitelocator

4 Support for You

Caregiving is emotionally hard — these offer connection and guidance.

Family Caregiver Alliance
Education, support, and state-by-state resource navigation.
→ www.caregiver.org

Condition-Specific Caregiver Help
Groups like the Alzheimer’s Association (1-800-272-3900) offer free 24/7 caregiver support.
→ www.alz.org/help-support

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Don’t fall for “caregiver grant” offers that charge a
fee — real programs are free. And don’t wait until
you’re burned out to ask for respite; taking breaks
helps both you and the person you care for.

Ask your state Medicaid office specifically about
“self-directed” or “consumer-directed” care — it’s
how many family members get paid to provide care
they’re already giving.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

you, use the personalized AI search or ask in the Questions area, and we’ll help you find the closest options.

Lesko_Help_HC12_Medical_Bill_Assistance_.title: Medical Bill Financial Assistance
Lesko_Help_HC12_Medical_Bill_Assistance_.tip:
Never put a big medical bill on a high-interest credit
card or a medical credit card before applying for
charity care — once it’s on a card, the hospital’s
assistance no longer applies. And debt collectors
must pause while your charity-care application is
pending.

Apply for charity care even if the bill already arrived
or feels old — it can still be forgiven. Always ask for
an itemized bill first; billing errors are common and
can lower what you owe before assistance is even
calculated.

Lesko_Help_HC12_Medical_Bill_Assistance_.text:
Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Medical Bill Financial Assistance
Facing a medical bill you can’t pay? Hospitals are often legally required to forgive or reduce bills, and
charities help cover treatment costs. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the box once
you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Don’t ignore a medical bill or put it on a credit card before checking these options. Nonprofit hospitals
must offer financial assistance (“charity care”), and asking can wipe out or shrink your bill — even after
it’s sent.

1 Ask the Hospital for Charity Care

Nonprofit hospitals are required by law to have a financial assistance policy that can reduce or erase your bill.

Dollar For — Hospital Bill Help
A free nonprofit that checks if you qualify for hospital charity care and helps you apply.
→ dollarfor.org

Ask for the “Financial Assistance Policy”
Call the hospital billing department and request their Financial Assistance Policy application. They must
provide it; collections pause while it’s pending.
→ Call your hospital's billing department

2 Get Help With Treatment Costs

Charities provide grants for copays, treatment, and related costs for many conditions.

PAN Foundation
Grants to help with copays and out-of-pocket costs for dozens of conditions.
→ www.panfoundation.org

Patient Advocate Foundation
Free case managers plus a co-pay relief fund to help with medical costs.
→ www.patientadvocate.org

HealthWell Foundation
Grants for copays, premiums, and out-of-pocket costs for many illnesses.
→ www.healthwellfoundation.org

3 Check Your Bill for Errors

Medical bills are often wrong. Your legal rights can lower what you owe.

No Surprises Act — Fight Surprise Bills
Protects you from many surprise out-of-network charges. If a bill exceeds your Good Faith Estimate by
$400+, you can dispute it.
→ www.cms.gov/medical-bill-rights

Request an Itemized Bill
Always ask for a line-by-line itemized bill and check for errors or duplicate charges before paying.
→ Ask your provider for an itemized bill

4 Set Up Affordable Payments

If you do owe, you have options besides paying it all at once.

Ask for a Payment Plan or Discount
Many providers offer interest-free payment plans or a discount if you ask — especially for paying cash.
→ Ask your provider's billing office

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Never put a big medical bill on a high-interest credit
card or a medical credit card before applying for
charity care — once it’s on a card, the hospital’s
assistance no longer applies. And debt collectors
must pause while your charity-care application is
pending.

Apply for charity care even if the bill already arrived
or feels old — it can still be forgiven. Always ask for
an itemized bill first; billing errors are common and
can lower what you owe before assistance is even
calculated.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

The GI Bill can cover tuition, housing, and books, and unused benefits can sometimes transfer to a
spouse or child. Apply free on VA.gov — never pay a service to “process” your education benefits.

Benefits cover many paths, not just college.

→ www.va.gov/education/about-gi-bill-benefits/how-to-use-benefits/on-the-job-training-
apprenticeships

Vocational Rehabilitation (VR&E / Chapter 31)
Free training, education, and job help for veterans with service-connected disabilities.
→ www.va.gov/careers-employment/vocational-rehabilitation

Programs that add to your benefits.

Yellow Ribbon Program
Helps cover tuition above the GI Bill cap at participating schools.
→ www.va.gov/education/about-gi-bill-benefits/post-9-11/yellow-ribbon-program

VetSuccess on Campus
Free on-campus support to help veterans succeed in school.
→ www.va.gov/careers-employment/vocational-rehabilitation/programs/vetsuccess-on-campus

Your education benefits can help your loved ones too.

Transfer GI Bill to Family
Eligible service members can transfer unused benefits to a spouse or children.
→ www.va.gov/education/transfer-post-9-11-gi-bill-benefits

Survivors’ & Dependents’ Education (DEA / Fry)
Education benefits for families of veterans who died or are permanently disabled.
→ www.va.gov/education/survivor-dependent-benefits

recruit veterans for their GI Bill money — check
graduation and job rates with the GI Bill Comparison
Tool, and prefer accredited public colleges.

Q U I C K G U I D E · TA X E S H E L P G U I D A N C E

Free Tax Filing
You should never have to pay to file your taxes. Millions qualify to file free — online or with free in-
person help — and keep their whole refund. Below are the official free options. Tick the box once
you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

About 100 million people can file free but most don’t know it. Note: the IRS “Direct File” pilot was
canceled for 2026 — use the options below instead. Never pay a preparer who takes a cut of your
refund.

1

File Free Online

Free guided software if your income is under the limit.

IRS Free File
Free guided tax software if your income is $89,000 or less. Available only through IRS.gov.
→ www.irs.gov/file-your-taxes-for-free

Free File Fillable Forms
Free electronic forms for any income level if you’re comfortable doing your own return.
→ www.irs.gov/e-file-providers/free-file-fillable-forms

2 Free In-Person Help

IRS-certified volunteers prepare your return for free.

VITA — Volunteer Income Tax Assistance
Free tax prep for people generally earning under ~$67,000, people with disabilities, and limited-English
speakers.
→ www.irs.gov/individuals/free-tax-return-preparation-for-qualifying-taxpayers 1-800-906-9887

AARP Foundation Tax-Aide
Free tax help, with a focus on people 50+ and lower incomes. No AARP membership needed.
→ www.aarp.org/money/taxes/aarp_taxaide

TCE — Tax Counseling for the Elderly
Free help for those 60+, specializing in pension and retirement questions.
→ www.irs.gov/individuals/free-tax-return-preparation-for-qualifying-taxpayers

3 Free Help Online & for Military

Virtual prep and a no-income-limit option for military.

GetYourRefund
Free virtual tax prep connecting you with VITA volunteers online.
→ www.getyourrefund.org

MilTax — Military
Free filing for service members and many veterans, with no income limit.
→ www.militaryonesource.mil/financial-legal/taxes/miltax-military-tax-services

4 Don’t Miss Your Refund

Filing free also unlocks valuable refundable credits.

Claim the EITC & Child Tax Credit
Even if you owe no tax, filing can get you thousands back. See the Tax Credits guide.
→ See: Tax Credits You May Be Missing guide

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Avoid “refund anticipation” loans and preparers who
take a percentage of your refund — they eat into
money that’s yours. The free options above are safe
and keep 100% of your refund.

Use a VITA or AARP Tax-Aide site if your return
involves the EITC — certified volunteers catch
mistakes and make sure you get every dollar you’re
owed.

Entrepreneurs with disabilities have dedicated funding, free expert help, and programs that let you

Free Expert Help

Specialists who understand both business and disability.

National Disability Institute — Small Business Hub
Free business planning, financial coaching, and grant access for entrepreneurs with disabilities.
→ www.nationaldisabilityinstitute.org/achieve-small-business-success

Free guidance on self-employment, financing, and accommodations.
→ askjan.org/topics/entrepreneurship.cfm

2 State Vocational Rehabilitation

VR agencies can fund and support self-employment goals.

Vocational Rehabilitation Self-Employment
Your state VR agency may help fund equipment, training, and startup costs for a business.
→ rsa.ed.gov/about/states

3 Protect Your Benefits

Start a business without automatically losing SSI/SSDI.

SSA PASS Plan (Plan to Achieve Self-Support)
Lets you set aside income/resources toward a work goal — like starting a business — without losing SSI.
→ www.ssa.gov/disabilityresearch/wi/pass.htm

ABLE Accounts
Tax-advantaged savings that don’t count against most benefit limits — useful for business savings.
→ www.ablenrc.org

4 Funding & Grants

Loans and grants that support disabled entrepreneurs.

Disability Opportunity Fund (CDFI)
Loans and technical help for businesses owned by people with disabilities.
→ thedof.org

NASE Growth Grants
Up to $4,000 grants for self-employed members (open to disabled entrepreneurs).
→ www.nase.org/become-a-member/grants-and-scholarships/business-development-grants

And before earning business income, check how it
affects your benefits — a free benefits counselor

Know your rights with lenders and debt collectors.

dementia or cure brain conditions with supplements
or special programs — these aren’t proven. Trust the
established nonprofits and .gov sources above.

after a diagnosis. They can explain what to expect,
connect you with support groups, and point you to
financial help you may not know exists.

Low-cost refurbished computers and low-cost internet for income-eligible people.

Q U I C K G U I D E · B O O S T Y O U R C A R E E R

Scholarships & Grants
Free money for school and training is everywhere — if you know where to look. Below are trusted, free
national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Real scholarships are always free to apply for. The #1 rule: never pay a fee to search for or “win” a
scholarship. The free tools below list the same opportunities paid services charge for.

1

Free Scholarship Search Tools

Trusted, free databases of scholarships.

CareerOneStop Scholarship Finder
A free, official Department of Labor database of 9,000+ scholarships and grants.
→ www.careeronestop.org/Toolkit/Training/find-scholarships.aspx

Federal Student Aid — Scholarships
Government guidance on finding and winning scholarships.
→ studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/scholarships

2 Don’t Forget Grants

Grants are need-based free money — start with the FAFSA.

File the FAFSA
Unlocks Pell and state grants. See the Financial Aid Basics guide.
→ studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa

Pell Grant
Up to ~$7,395/year you never repay.
→ studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/grants/pell

3 Look Close to Home

Local and niche scholarships have less competition.

Local & Community Scholarships
Check your school counselor, library, employer, church, and local clubs — smaller scholarships are easier
to win.
→ Ask your school counselor or library

Scholarships for Your Situation
Many scholarships target specific careers, backgrounds, or communities. Search your field/background +
“scholarship.”
→ Search your situation + 'scholarship'

4 Apply Smart

A little strategy wins more money.

Reuse One Strong Essay
Write one solid essay you can adapt, and apply to many smaller scholarships — volume wins.
→ Apply to many smaller scholarships

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Never pay for a scholarship search or to “release” a
scholarship you’ve “won” — those are scams. The
CareerOneStop database is free and lists the same
scholarships paid sites do.

Apply to lots of small, local scholarships rather than
only the big famous ones — they have far less
competition, and several $500 awards add up fast.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

VA Disability Compensation & Pension
If you have a service-connected condition — or low income as a wartime veteran — you may qualify

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Tax-free monthly pay for service-connected conditions.

Apply for Disability Compensation
Tax-free monthly pay for injuries or illnesses connected to your service.
→ www.va.gov/disability

PACT Act — Toxic Exposure
If you were exposed to burn pits, Agent Orange, or other toxins, you may now qualify. File a claim.
→ www.va.gov/resources/the-pact-act-and-your-va-benefits

How to apply and improve your odds.

Get Free Help From a VSO
Accredited officers file and strengthen your claim for free.
→ www.va.gov/get-help-from-accredited-representative

Fully Developed Claim
Submitting all evidence up front speeds up your decision.
→ www.va.gov/disability/how-to-file-claim

Needs-based, tax-free income for wartime veterans.

VA Pension
Tax-free monthly income for low-income wartime veterans 65+ or disabled.
→ www.va.gov/pension

Aid & Attendance
Extra pension if you need help with daily activities or are housebound.
→ www.va.gov/pension/aid-attendance-housebound

You have strong appeal rights — use them.

Appeal a VA Decision
Many claims succeed on appeal. A VSO can help you choose the right appeal option for free.
→ www.va.gov/decision-reviews

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

Never pay a company a percentage of your back pay
to file — VSOs do it free, and charging for initial claim
prep is illegal. You can also receive VA disability and
Social Security at the same time.

Even an old or previously denied condition may now
qualify, especially under the PACT Act. Talk to a VSO

Veterans get dedicated business training, certification, and funding to help them succeed as
entrepreneurs. Below are trusted national resources. Tick the box once you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Much of this support is free, and veteran certification can unlock set-aside government contracts.
Beware of anyone charging big fees for “veteran business grants.”

Free Veteran Business Training

Programs built specifically for veteran entrepreneurs.

Free certification to compete for veteran set-aside federal contracts.

assistance-programs

Loans and grants that support veteran-owned businesses.

Food & Grocery Help
If your income doesn’t cover groceries every month, you’re not alone — and real help exists. Federal
benefits and community food programs can put food on your table this week and every month. Tick
the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Many people who qualify never apply because they don’t know these programs exist. There’s no risk in
checking your eligibility, and applying is always free. Your local food bank can even help you fill out the
forms.

1 Monthly Grocery Benefits (SNAP)

SNAP (formerly food stamps) loads money onto a card you use like debit at grocery stores and many farmers
markets. It’s the biggest food program in the country.

SNAP — How to Apply
Apply through your state. Income limit is generally around 130% of the federal poverty level, with higher
limits for households with seniors or disabled members.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility

Find Your State SNAP Office
Each state runs its own application. This finds your state’s office and online application.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/state-directory

2 Food Right Now (Food Banks & Pantries)

Food banks give out free groceries — shelf-stable items, fresh produce, dairy, sometimes meat. Most serve
anyone in their community who asks.

near you.
→ www.feedingamerica.org/find-your-local-foodbank

211 — Local Food Help
Call or search to find pantries, hot meals, and food programs in your area.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

3 For Pregnant Women, Babies & Young Kids (WIC)

WIC provides healthy foods, formula, nutrition help, and breastfeeding support for families with young
children.

WIC — Women, Infants & Children
Free healthy groceries and support if you’re pregnant, recently had a baby, or have a child under 5, and
meet income rules (or get SNAP, Medicaid, or TANF).
→ www.fns.usda.gov/wic

4 Help for Kids & Seniors

Targeted programs feed children during the school year and summer, and provide groceries for older adults.

Free & Reduced-Price School Meals
Your child may qualify for free or low-cost meals at school and food over the summer. Ask your child’s
school or district office.
→ Ask your child’s school

Senior Food Programs
Food help for adults 60+, including the Commodity Supplemental Food Program. Find options through the
Eldercare Locator.
→ eldercare.acl.gov or call 1-800-677-1110

FDPIR — Food Distribution on Indian Reservations
Monthly packages of healthy food for eligible households on or near reservations.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/fdpir

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Be careful of sites that charge a fee to “apply for
SNAP” or sell an EBT card. Applying for SNAP, WIC,
and food bank help is always free through
official .gov sites and nonprofits.

Food banks serve everyone — you don’t need to be
on benefits to use them, and you can use them while
your SNAP application is being processed. Don’t wait
until the cupboard is empty.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Q U I C K G U I D E · F I N D L E G A L H E L P

Know Your Consumer Rights
Being treated unfairly by a company, debt collector, or scammer? You have powerful federal rights —
and free ways to fight back. Below are the official resources. Tick the box once you’ve checked each
one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Federal agencies exist to protect you, and complaining to them is free and often effective. Companies
frequently fix problems fast once a regulator is involved. Never pay anyone who promises to “recover”
scam money for a fee.

1 Money & Debt Protections

Your rights with banks, lenders, and debt collectors.

CFPB — File a Complaint
The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau helps with banks, loans, credit, and debt collectors. Companies
usually must respond.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint

Debt Collector Rules (FDCPA)
Collectors can’t harass you, call at all hours, or lie. Know your rights and report violations.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/debt-collection

2 Scams & Unfair Business

Report fraud and unfair practices to the nation’s consumer watchdog.

FTC — Report Fraud
Report scams, identity theft, and unfair business practices, and get a recovery plan.
→ reportfraud.ftc.gov

IdentityTheft.gov
If your identity was stolen, get a free step-by-step recovery plan.
→ www.identitytheft.gov

3 Your Credit Rights

Check and fix your credit for free.

Free Credit Reports
Get your credit reports free every week from all three bureaus.
→ www.annualcreditreport.com

Dispute Credit Errors
You have the right to dispute and fix errors on your credit report for free.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-do-i-dispute-an-error-on-my-credit-report-en-314

4 More Help

Other trusted places to resolve consumer problems.

State Attorney General & Consumer Protection
Your state AG handles many consumer complaints. Search your state + “attorney general consumer
complaint.”
→ Search your state + 'attorney general consumer protection'

USA.gov — Consumer Help
The government’s hub for consumer complaints and your rights.
→ www.usa.gov/consumer-complaints

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

If someone contacts you promising to recover
money you lost to a scam — for a fee — that’s a
second scam. Real government help (FTC, CFPB) is
always free. Never pay to file a complaint.

Put complaints in writing and keep records of every
call and letter. A complaint to the CFPB or FTC
creates a paper trail that often gets results when
calling the company didn’t.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Search a national directory of treatment programs, including low-cost and sliding-scale options.

Free meetings worldwide for anyone who wants to stop drinking. Find local and online meetings.

Free peer support meetings for recovery from drug addiction.

Free, science-based recovery meetings and tools, in person and online.

Free support groups for families and friends of people with a drinking problem.
→ al-anon.org

SAMHSA — Find Support
Plain guidance for taking the first steps, for you or a loved one.
→ www.findsupport.gov

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Be wary of for-profit “rehab” centers that pressure
you, promise guaranteed cures, or charge huge
upfront fees. Start with the free SAMHSA helpline,
which gives unbiased referrals.

You don’t have to wait until you “hit bottom.” Calling

site. Avoid “grant services” that charge to enter you
— legitimate corporate grants are always free to
apply for, and deadlines/amounts change, so verify

you’d use the money for, and basic numbers. Then
you can apply to many grants quickly instead of
starting over each time.

Lesko_Help_04_Debt_Help_Credit_Counselin.title: Debt Help & Credit Counseling
Lesko_Help_04_Debt_Help_Credit_Counselin.tip:
If a company asks for a big fee before doing
anything, “guarantees” it can wipe out your debt, or
tells you to stop paying and stop talking to creditors
— walk away. The FTC shut down a $100M debt scam
in 2025 that did exactly this.

Start with a free NFCC counseling session before
signing anything. A good counselor will lay out all
your options — including ones that cost you nothing
— with no pressure to enroll.

resources.name: Drowning in credit card or other debt? Free, trustworthy nonprofit cou
resources.description: Drowning in credit card or other debt? Free, trustworthy nonprofit counselors can help you build a plan, lower your interest, and deal with creditors — without the traps of for-profit “debt relief” companies. Tick the box once you’ve contacted each one. Real nonprofit credit counseling is low-cost or free and never charges large upfront fees. Be very careful with companies that promise to “erase” your debt, guarantee results, or tell you to stop paying your creditors — those are the classic signs of a scam. Free Nonprofit Credit Counseling Certified counselors review your full situation for free and help you choose a path. Look for the NFCC network — member agencies don’t charge upfront fees. NFCC — National Foundation for Credit Counseling The nation’s largest nonprofit credit counseling network. Connect with a certified counselor who works with you and your lenders.

resources.description: Search for a vetted nonprofit counseling agency near you or by phone.

resources.description: A counselor may set up a Debt Management Plan (DMP) — one monthly payment, often with lower interest rates negotiated with your creditors. Ask About a Debt Management Plan Through an NFCC counselor, a DMP can roll your debts into one affordable payment and may lower your interest. A safer, cheaper alternative to for-profit debt settlement.

Lesko_Help_HC07_Dental_Care_Quick_Guide.title: Free & Low-Cost Dental Care
Lesko_Help_HC07_Dental_Care_Quick_Guide.watch_out:
advertised “dental grants” that still leave you with a big bill. The programs below are
nonprofits, dental schools, and government services — not sales pitches. A real program never charges a
fee just to apply.

1

Find Free & Low-Cost Clinics Near You

National directories listing community clinics, sliding-scale dentists, and low-cost programs by location.

NeedyMeds — Free & Low-Cost Clinics
A national directory of free and reduced-cost dental clinics. Search by location.
→ www.needymeds.org/free-clinics

Health Center Finder — HRSA
Federally funded health centers offer dental care on a sliding fee scale based on income.
→ findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov

FindHelp.org — Dental Search
Enter your ZIP code and search “dental” for local free or low-cost care.
→ www.findhelp.org

2 Volunteer Dentists Through Dental Lifeline

A national network connecting volunteer dentists with people who qualify — often for free comprehensive
treatment.

Dental Lifeline Network — Donated Dental Services
Free treatment for people who are elderly, have a disability, or are medically fragile. Check your state
program and eligibility.
→ dentallifeline.org/our-state-programs

3 Dental Schools — Low-Cost, Supervised Care

Dental and hygiene schools offer treatment at a fraction of the usual cost, done by students under expert
supervision.

Dental Schools — ADA Directory
Find accredited dental schools that run low-cost clinics open to the public.
→ www.ada.org

Dental Hygiene Programs — ADHA
Hygiene schools offer very low-cost cleanings, X-rays, and preventive care.
→ www.adha.org

4 Government & Public Coverage

Public programs cover dental care for many adults and children — worth checking even if you think you don’t
qualify.

Medicaid & CHIP Dental Benefits
Children always get dental coverage; many states cover adults too.
→ www.medicaid.gov/medicaid/benefits/dental-care

InsureKidsNow — Find a Dentist
A federal tool to find dentists who accept Medicaid and CHIP for children.
→ www.insurekidsnow.gov

Eldercare Locator — For Seniors
Connects you with local agencies that may offer dental help and referrals.
→ eldercare.acl.gov or call 1-800-677-1110

5 Special Situations

Targeted programs for children, survivors of violence, and veterans.

America’s ToothFairy — Kids’ Dental Care
Connects families with free and low-cost dental care for children.
→ www.americastoothfairy.org

Give Back a Smile — Survivors of Violence
Free restorative dental care for survivors of domestic and sexual violence.
→ aacdcharitablefoundation.org

VA Dental Care — For Veterans
Eligible veterans get VA dental benefits; others may use the VA Dental Insurance Program.
→ www.va.gov/health-care/about-va-health-benefits/dental-care

⚠ WATC H OUT FOR

★

front. Real programs don’t charge you to apply. Stick
to .gov, .org, dental schools, and the directories
above.

Call more than one program. Funding and waiting
lists change constantly — if one says no, the next
may say yes. Keep a simple list of who you called and
what they said.

Q U I C K G U I D E · S E N I O R S & D I S A B I L I T I E S

Disability Benefits & Income
Living with a disability that limits work? Federal programs provide monthly income and health
coverage — and you can save without losing benefits. Below are the main national starting points. Tick
the box once you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

The two main programs are SSDI (based on work history) and SSI (based on low income). Applying is
free — never pay upfront to file. If you’re denied at first (many are), you can appeal, and free help exists.

1 Monthly Income Benefits

The two main federal disability income programs.

SSDI — Social Security Disability Insurance
Monthly benefits if you worked and paid Social Security but can no longer work due to disability.
→ www.ssa.gov/benefits/disability 1-800-772-1213

SSI — Supplemental Security Income
Monthly payments for people with disabilities (and seniors) who have little income or resources.
→ www.ssa.gov/ssi

2 Health Coverage

Disability benefits open the door to health coverage.

Medicaid & Medicare
SSI usually brings Medicaid; SSDI brings Medicare after a waiting period. Check your eligibility.
→ www.medicaid.gov/medicaid/eligibility/index.html

3 Apply & Appeal

How to file — and what to do if you’re denied.

Apply for Disability
Apply online, by phone, or in person. Gather medical records to support your claim.
→ www.ssa.gov/applyfordisability

Free Help & Appeals
Many are denied first time. Free legal aid and disability advocates can help you appeal; most lawyers only
get paid if you win.
→ www.lawhelp.org

4 Save Without Losing Benefits

Special accounts let you build savings safely.

ABLE Accounts
Tax-advantaged savings that don’t count against SSI/Medicaid limits, for people disabled before age 46.
→ www.ablenrc.org

Work Incentives (Ticket to Work)
Try working without immediately losing benefits, through free SSA work programs.
→ choosework.ssa.gov 1-866-968-7842

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Never pay a large upfront fee to “get approved” for
disability — reputable disability attorneys are only
paid a capped amount if you win. Be wary of anyone
guaranteeing approval.

Apply as soon as your condition prevents work, and
keep detailed medical records — they’re the heart of
a strong claim. If denied, appeal; many people are
approved only after appealing with help.

Buying a Home — Grants & Programs
Think you can’t afford to buy? Government-backed loans and down-payment help make
homeownership possible with little or even no money down. Below are the main national programs.
Tick the box once you’ve looked into each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

There is no single national “free house” grant — real help is a stack of low-down-payment loans, state

approved counselor will guide you for free.

1

Low- & No-Down-Payment Loans

These federal loan programs let you buy with little or nothing down, with easier credit rules than regular
mortgages.

FHA Loans
As little as 3.5% down with flexible credit. The most common first-time buyer loan. Offered by approved
lenders.
→ www.hud.gov/buying/loans

USDA Rural Loans
Zero down payment for homes in eligible rural and many suburban areas. Check the address on the
eligibility map.
→ www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/single-family-housing-programs

VA Loans — Veterans & Service Members
Zero down, no ongoing mortgage insurance, for eligible veterans, service members, and some surviving
spouses.
→ www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans

2 Down Payment & Closing Cost Help

Every state runs a Housing Finance Agency offering grants and forgivable loans — often $5,000–$15,000+ —
for first-time buyers.

Find Your State Housing Finance Agency
Each state offers first-time buyer grants, low-interest loans, and closing-cost help. Find yours here.
→ www.ncsha.org/housing-help

HUD — Local Homebuying Programs
HUD’s state-by-state list of down-payment assistance and homebuying programs.
→ www.hud.gov/buying/local-buying-programs

Discounts and programs for specific workers and first-time buyers.

Teachers, law enforcement, firefighters, and EMTs can buy eligible HUD homes at 50% off in revitalization
areas (live there 3 years).
→ www.hud.gov/program_offices/housing/sfh/reo/goodn/gnndabot

HUD Homes for Sale
Browse HUD-owned homes for sale, sometimes below market price.
→ www.hudhomestore.gov

4 Get Free Expert Help First

A HUD-approved housing counselor walks you through your budget, credit, and which programs fit — for free.

HUD-Approved Housing Counselor
Free guidance on buying, budgeting, and qualifying for assistance. Find one near you.
→ www.hud.gov/findacounselor

Homebuyer Education Courses
Many grants require a short homebuyer course — your state HFA or a HUD counselor can point you to a
free or low-cost one.
→ Ask your HUD counselor or state HFA

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Skip anyone advertising a guaranteed “$25,000
buyer grant” for an upfront fee. Real down-payment

house-hunting. They’ll help you fix your credit, set a

Lesko_Help_HC10_Vision_Hearing_Care_Quic.tip:
Be cautious of high-pressure sales for expensive
hearing aids — for many people, the new over-the-
counter options work well at a fraction of the price.
Always get a written eyeglass prescription so you
can shop around.

Ask your eye doctor for a copy of your prescription
— they’re required to give it to you — then buy
glasses cheaply online. For hearing, try over-the-
counter aids before spending thousands.

Lesko_Help_FC_B3_Free_Low_Cost_Seniors_Q.tip:
You usually have to ask for senior discounts —
they’re rarely automatic. And avoid “senior discount”
sites that charge a membership; legitimate
discounts are free just for being your age.

Always ask “Is there a senior discount?” — transit,
pharmacies, stores, and entertainment often have
them. Combined with benefit programs, the savings

Free & Low-Cost Help for Seniors
Stretching a fixed income? Seniors qualify for discounts and free programs on phones, transport,
fitness, taxes, and more. Below are the main national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve checked
each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Lots of everyday savings go unclaimed simply because people don’t ask. The programs below are free or
low-cost — and many you qualify for just by being 60 or 65+.

1 Phone, Internet & Utilities

Lower your monthly bills.

Lifeline — Phone/Internet Discount
Monthly discount on phone or internet. See the Phone & Internet guide.
→ www.lifelinesupport.org

LIHEAP — Energy Help
Help paying heating and cooling bills.
→ www.acf.hhs.gov/ocs/programs/liheap 1-866-674-6327

2 Food & Health Savings

Free food programs and ways to cut health costs.

Senior Food & Farmers Market Coupons
Free groceries and produce coupons for older adults. See the Healthy Food guide.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/sfmnp

Prescription Savings
Cut drug costs with Extra Help and discount tools. See the Prescription guide.
→ www.ssa.gov/medicare/part-d-extra-help

3 Get Around & Stay Active

Affordable transport and free fitness.

Senior Transportation
Free or low-cost rides to appointments and errands via the Eldercare Locator.
→ eldercare.acl.gov 1-800-677-1110

Free Senior Fitness (SilverSneakers)
Many Medicare plans include free gym membership. Ask your plan.
→ www.silversneakers.com

4 Free Taxes, Discounts & Fun

More everyday savings.

Free Tax Help (AARP Tax-Aide / TCE)
Free tax prep focused on seniors. See the Free Tax Filing guide.
→ www.aarp.org/money/taxes/aarp_taxaide

→ www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/passes.htm

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

You usually have to ask for senior discounts —
they’re rarely automatic. And avoid “senior discount”
sites that charge a membership; legitimate
discounts are free just for being your age.

Always ask “Is there a senior discount?” — transit,
pharmacies, stores, and entertainment often have
them. Combined with benefit programs, the savings
add up fast on a fixed income.

Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Prescription Drug Help
Can’t afford your medications? You may be able to get them free or far cheaper through manufacturer
programs, nonprofits, and discount tools. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the box once
you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Never skip or split doses to save money before checking these options — many people get the very
same drug free or for a few dollars. Always ask your pharmacist about generics, too.

1

Find Programs for Your Medication

These directories match you to patient-assistance programs based on the exact drug you take.

NeedyMeds
A free database of patient-assistance programs, plus a discount drug card and free-clinic directory.
→ www.needymeds.org

RxAssist
A directory of drug-company programs that give medicines free or cheaply to people who qualify.
→ www.rxassist.org

Medicine Assistance Tool (PhRMA)
Search hundreds of manufacturer assistance programs in one place.
→ medicineassistancetool.org

2 Lower the Price at the Pharmacy

Discount tools and low-cost generics can dramatically cut what you pay, even without insurance.

GoodRx — Compare & Save
Free coupons and price comparisons that can cut prescription costs sharply. No membership needed.
→ www.goodrx.com

Cost Plus Drugs
An online pharmacy selling many generics at very low, transparent prices.
→ costplusdrugs.com

Low-Cost Generic Lists
Many pharmacies sell common generics for about $4. Ask your pharmacy for its discount generic list.
→ Ask your pharmacy

3 Free Medicine for Those Who Qualify

Nonprofits and clinics provide free medications to low-income and uninsured patients.

SIRUM — Free Surplus Medicine
A nonprofit that redirects unused, unexpired medicine to patients in need.
→ sirum.org/get-medications

Free & Charitable Clinics
Many free clinics include prescription assistance. Find one near you.
→ www.needymeds.org/free-clinics

4 Help for Medicare & Seniors

Special programs lower drug costs for people on Medicare.

Medicare Extra Help (Low-Income Subsidy)
Federal help paying Part D drug costs for people with limited income (up to 150% of poverty level).
→ www.ssa.gov/medicare/part-d-extra-help

State Pharmaceutical Assistance Programs
Some states help residents pay for medications. Ask your SHIP counselor (see the Medicare guide).
→ www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/drug-costs

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

access drug discounts — GoodRx and the programs

Behind on rent or facing eviction? Acting fast matters — free legal help and local rental assistance can
keep you housed. Below are the most trusted national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve
contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

The big federal pandemic rental program (ERA2) ended in 2025, so rental help now comes through local
programs, charities, and legal aid. Never pay a fee to apply for rental assistance — real programs are free.
If you have a court date, get legal help right away.

1

Find Local Rental Assistance

Federal money now flows through state and local programs. These official tools point you to what’s open near
you.

CFPB — Find Rental Assistance Near You
The official government tool that lists rental and utility assistance programs by state, county, and city.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/coronavirus/mortgage-and-housing-assistance/renter-protections/
find-help-with-rent-and-utilities

211 — Local Rent Help
Call or search to find emergency rent funds, charities, and housing help in your area.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

2 Free Legal Help to Fight Eviction

If you’ve gotten an eviction notice or court date, a free tenant lawyer can often stop or delay it, or get back
rent waived.

HUD Eviction Protection — Free Tenant Legal Aid
Free legal services for low-income tenants at risk of eviction, funded by HUD. Find a provider through legal
aid below.
→ www.lawhelp.org

Legal Services Corporation — Find Legal Aid
Find your local free legal aid office for help with eviction, lease problems, and tenant rights.
→ www.lsc.gov/about-lsc/what-legal-aid/get-legal-help

3 Talk to a HUD Housing Counselor

Free, expert counselors help you understand your options, contact your landlord, and find assistance — at no
cost.

HUD-Approved Housing Counseling
Free counseling on renting, eviction, and avoiding homelessness. Find a HUD-approved counselor near
you.
→ www.hud.gov/findacounselor

HUD Housing Counselor Line
Call to be connected with a free local housing counselor.
→ 1-800-569-4287

4 Know Your Rights

Understanding the rules in your state can buy you time and protect you from illegal eviction.

USA.gov — Tenant Rights
Plain-language overview of renter rights and where to report problems in your state.
→ www.usa.gov/housing-rental-issues

Find Your Local Public Housing Agency
For Section 8, public housing waitlists, and emergency housing options.
→ www.hud.gov/helping-americans/public-housing-agency-contact-information

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Old sites still say you can apply for the federal “ERA”
or “Emergency Rental Assistance” program — that
federal round ended in 2025. Use the CFPB tool and
211 to find what’s actually open. Never pay an upfront
fee.

If you have an eviction court date, get free legal help
immediately — even one day matters. Many tenants
who show up with a lawyer avoid eviction or get
extra time to move.

Lesko_Help_CB_C01_Financial_Aid_Basics_Q.text:
Q U I C K G U I D E · B O O S T Y O U R C A R E E R

Financial Aid Basics — Federal & State
Going back to school or training? Federal and state financial aid can cover much of the cost — and a
lot of it is free money you never repay. Below are the official starting points. Tick the box once you’ve
done each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

The single most important step is filing the FAFSA — it’s free and unlocks grants, work-study, and loans.
Never pay a service to file it for you; the official site is free.

1 Start With the FAFSA

One free form unlocks most financial aid, including free grants.

File the FAFSA — Free
The key to federal and state aid. “FAFSA” literally means FREE Application — never pay to file it.
→ studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa

StudentAid.gov — Aid Overview
Understand grants, work-study, and loans before you borrow.
→ studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types

2 Free Money: Grants

Grants don’t have to be repaid — always max these out first.

Federal Pell Grant
Up to about $7,395/year for students with financial need. A new “Workforce Pell” (starting July 2026) also
covers shorter job-training programs.
→ studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/grants/pell

State Grant Programs
Your state likely has its own grants. Filing the FAFSA often applies for these automatically.
→ studentaid.gov/resources/state-contacts

3 Work-Study & Smart Borrowing

Earn while you learn, and borrow wisely if you must.

Federal Work-Study
Part-time jobs to help pay for school, arranged through your college.
→ studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/work-study

Federal Loans (Borrow Last)
If you must borrow, federal loans have better terms than private ones. See the Student Loan Help guide.
→ See: Student Loan Help guide

4 Get Free Help Applying

Free, trustworthy help with the FAFSA and aid.

Federal Student Aid Help
Free help by phone or chat with your FAFSA and aid questions.
→ studentaid.gov/help-center/contact 1-800-433-3243

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Never pay to file the FAFSA — the real site is
studentaid.gov and it’s free. Avoid “scholarship” or
“aid” services that charge fees or guarantee money;
legitimate aid never works that way.

File the FAFSA as early as you can each year — some
aid is first-come, first-served, and filing early can
mean more free grant money.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Need help where you live?

This guide covers federal aid. For your state’s grants and deadlines, use the personalized AI search or ask in
the Questions area, and we’ll help you find them.

Lesko_Help_FC_B1_18_Things_Seniors_Quick.tip:
Seniors are the #1 target for scams. Medicare, Social
Security, and the IRS will never call to demand
payment or your number — hang up and call the
official line yourself. Never pay to “claim” free
benefits.

Start with one call to the Eldercare Locator or a
BenefitsCheckUp online — either can reveal
thousands of dollars in benefits you may be missing,
then point you to free local help to apply.

Q U I C K G U I D E · S E N I O R S & D I S A B I L I T I E S

18 Things Every Senior Should Know
There’s a huge amount of help for older adults — money, health, food, home, and more — that many
seniors never claim. Below are the key starting points, all free to explore. Tick the box once you’ve
checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

One free call to the Eldercare Locator (1-800-677-1110) can connect you to most of what’s below in your
area. Programs are free to apply for — never pay a “benefits consultant” for what you can get directly.

1 Start With One Free Call

The single best entry point to senior help nationwide.

Eldercare Locator
Free connection to local services: meals, transport, caregiver help, and more.
→ eldercare.acl.gov 1-800-677-1110

BenefitsCheckUp
Free tool that finds benefits you may qualify for, from medicine to food to utilities.
→ www.benefitscheckup.org

2 Money & Health Coverage

Income support and help with health costs.

Social Security & SSI
Retirement, disability, and SSI for those with low income. Check what you’re owed.
→ www.ssa.gov 1-800-772-1213

Medicare & Free SHIP Counseling
Free, unbiased Medicare help to cut costs. See the Medicare guide.
→ www.shiphelp.org SHIP: 1-877-839-2675

Medicare Savings & Extra Help
Programs that pay premiums and drug costs for limited incomes.
→ www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/medicare-savings-programs

3 Food, Home & Utilities

Everyday essentials made affordable.

Senior Meals & SNAP
Home-delivered/community meals and food benefits (easier rules for those 60+).
→ www.nutrition.gov/topics/food-assistance-programs/meals-seniors

LIHEAP & Weatherization
Help with energy bills and free home energy upgrades. See the Utility guide.
→ www.acf.hhs.gov/ocs/programs/liheap 1-866-674-6327

4 Protect Yourself

Stay safe from fraud and know where to turn.

Report Elder Fraud
Free help if you’re targeted by a scam (seniors are common targets).
→ ovc.ojp.gov/program/stop-elder-fraud DOJ Elder Fraud: 1-833-372-8311

Free Legal Help for Seniors
Legal aid for benefits, housing, and elder-law issues via the Eldercare Locator.
→ eldercare.acl.gov 1-800-677-1110

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Seniors are the #1 target for scams. Medicare, Social
Security, and the IRS will never call to demand
payment or your number — hang up and call the
official line yourself. Never pay to “claim” free
benefits.

Start with one call to the Eldercare Locator or a
BenefitsCheckUp online — either can reveal
thousands of dollars in benefits you may be missing,
then point you to free local help to apply.

N E E D H E L P W H E R E YO U L I V E ?

Need help where you live?

This guide covers national programs. For your local Area Agency on Aging and senior services, use the
personalized AI search or ask in the Questions area, and we’ll connect you.
